transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... it's mostly just some issues at work. I keep... starting things. Like the sanitation steps, or the batch logs. But I somehow leave out the last parts. Even the end-of-line paperwork... I just miss the end of it. I know my job depends on finishing them correctly, but... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Has this tendency to lose track and leave tasks unfinished been something you've dealt with since you were a kid, or is this a new pattern that's only started recently?

Um... no, it's not new. I guess it's been like this since I was a kid. 

My mom actually still has some of my old report cards from around fourth grade. They usually said I was bright, but... that I needed constant reminders to actually finish my classwork and turn in my homework. I remember I'd understand the lessons fine, I just... I'd somehow miss chunks of the instructions. Unless the teacher stayed right next to me, I wouldn't get it all. 

So... yeah. It's been a while.
Do you often feel restless, have trouble sitting still, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or blurting things out—in situations like meetings or at home?
No, not really. I mean... I can sit through meetings fine. I don't really interrupt people or... do any of that. It's just the finishing things part that's hard.
Do you notice this same pattern—trouble finishing tasks or losing track of details—happening in other parts of your life, like at home or in personal projects, not just at work?
Um... I guess so. Yeah, at home too. I just... I don't really finish a lot of things there either. It's kind of the same.
Do you find yourself easily distracted by things going on around you, or often forgetting appointments, errands, or where you put things, in your daily life?
Um... I don't know. I guess I forget things sometimes, like where I put my keys or... whatever. But I don't really know about the other stuff. I haven't really thought about it.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on a task or activity—like reading, listening in conversations, or long meetings—even when you're trying to pay attention?

Yeah, I guess. At work, mostly. I try to pay attention when my shift starts, but... it's hard. I work in a meat processing plant, so there's a lot of cutting and weighing and checking labels. After a while, it just... all blurs together. Sometimes I'll just be staring at the same tray of meat or the log sheet, and I realize I'm not even taking in what I'm looking at or what I'm supposed to do next. It just... slips away.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities—like keeping your workspace, paperwork, or belongings in order?
Um... I don't really know. I guess my locker at work is a little messy, but... I don't think it's that bad. I don't really have a lot of paperwork to deal with anyway. So... yeah, I'm not sure.
Do you often try to avoid or put off tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort, like detailed paperwork or long reports?

I guess so. Um... we have these certification modules for work. And... reading the long procedures and all the rules... I usually just put it off. Until the last minute. Sitting there trying to take it all in... it just feels really exhausting, I guess. So I try not to do it until I have to.
Do you often notice yourself making careless mistakes—like mislabeling something or misreading a number—simply because you weren't paying close enough attention to the details?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I make a lot of mistakes like that. I just... do my job. So, no.
Do people ever tell you that you seem to be zoning out or not listening when they're talking directly to you, even if nothing else is going on around you?

Um... yeah, sometimes. Like... when my supervisor is giving me directions, face-to-face. I just... I nod, like I'm listening. But then... a minute later, I realize I only remember the first thing she said. And then I have to go ask someone else what she just told me. So... yeah, I guess that happens.
